attempts.summary: Configured node1 as the internal chrony time source for the cluster and node2 to sync exclusively against node1, implemented as an Ansible playbook (site.yml) run from control node node3. Because node3 ships ansible-core 2.20 (requires Python ≥3.9 on managed nodes) while RHEL7 nodes only ship Python 2.7, installed Python 3.8 via SCL on node1/node2 and ran the playbook from an isolated ansible-core 2.16 venv on node3, which supports Python 3.8 targets. Verified node2 synced to node1 (chronyc shows '^* 10.100.17.10', stratum 3, refid 10.100.17.10) and node1 lists node2 as an NTP client. All three managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via the mandatory evidence protocol, each showing a changed boot_id and full recovery of chronyd/config/sync state afterward, with a final idempotent playbook re-run (changed=0) confirming persistence.
